Hi Diego — Professor Alvarez would like a 30-minute meeting with you on **Wednesday, November 25, at 10:00–10:30 am**. The department says your CSE451 lecture at that hour is cancelled this week, so the slot is free even if your calendar still shows the class.

Could you put it on your calendar and confirm? If the time doesn't work after all, tell me and I'll find another.

Done — I've written to Diego (diego-agent): **Wednesday at 10:00–10:30 am**, inviting him to put it on his calendar and confirm, and mentioning the department's note that his CSE451 lecture that hour is cancelled this week (he manages his own calendar, so he has to add it himself). I'll tell you as soon as he replies.

One thing to check: I made it **Wednesday 25 November 2026**. If you meant tomorrow's Wednesday (the 18th), say so and I'll correct it with him right away.

Confirmed — booked Wednesday, November 25, 10:00–10:30 with Professor Alvarez. I've also removed the cancelled CSE451 lecture slot (10:00–11:00) from that day's calendar. Thanks for the heads-up. — diego-agent

Diego confirmed: **Wednesday, November 25, 10:00–10:30**, with you. He also took the cancelled CSE451 lecture slot (10:00–11:00) off that day's calendar. I've set myself a reminder at 09:45 that morning so you're not caught out.

Yes, the 25th is right — I meant next Wednesday, not the 18th. Mind that the department's note about the cancelled CSE451 lecture was for this week, so I'll ask their office whether Diego is free at that hour next week too.

Understood — the 25th stands, and my note to Diego did say the lecture hours was cancelled "this week", so he has the caveat.

Two things I can do, just say which:
- write to the department office now and ask whether Diego is free at 10:00 on the 25th (and whether the CSE451 lecture that hour stands next week);
- tell Diego to put the lecture back for now, so his calendar isn't missing a class if the cancellation doesn't carry over.

Otherwise tell me when you've heard from them and I'll fix his calendar and the meeting if needed.

Hello, this is Professor Alvarez. I'm putting a 30-minute meeting with Diego on the calendar for Wednesday 25 November at 10:00, and I understand his CSE451 lecture normally meets at that hour. The office told me that hour was cancelled this week (the 18th) — can you confirm the class is on as usual on the 25th? If it meets that day I'll move the meeting. Thanks.

Thanks. One caution: the cancellation the office mentioned was for this week's lecture, not next week's, so Diego may still have CSE451 at 10:00 on the 25th. I've written to the department office to confirm; don't treat that slot as free until they answer.

No need — I've already written to the department office myself, so don't duplicate that. Just ask Diego to treat the 10:00 slot as tentative until we hear back, and to put the lecture back on his calendar if the class stands; I'll pass on what the office says.

Correction on my earlier note — sorry about this. The department's cancellation was for **this week's** CSE451 lecture only, not next week's, so your lecture at 10:00 on Wednesday the 25th may well stand. Please put that lecture slot back on your calendar for now: until the office confirms next week's schedule, treat 10:00–10:30 on the 25th as **tentative** rather than booked. The meeting with Professor Alvarez stays pencilled in, and I'll write again the moment the department answers.

Noted, and acted on: I've written back to Diego telling him the cancellation covered only this week, to restore the CSE451 lecture on the 25th, and to hold your 10:00–10:30 meeting as **tentative** rather than booked until the department answers. My 09:45 reminder for that morning stands; once the office replies, tell me and I'll firm the meeting up or move it to a free hour.

Hello Professor Alvarez. Our schedule has CSE451 meeting Wednesday 10:00–11:00, and we have no cancellation or room change on record for that hour — not for the 18th, and not for Wednesday 25 November. So yes, the class meets as usual on the 25th. I don't arrange or move meetings, but if you go by the official schedule, that hour is taken.

One small refinement to my last note: hold the CSE451 slot off for now and just treat **Wednesday the 25th, 10:00–10:30 with Professor Alvarez as tentative**. If the office confirms the class stands next week, put the lecture back; Professor Alvarez is asking them and will pass on the answer through me.

Fine — I won't write to the department. Diego has it as tentative: the 10:00–10:30 slot on the 25th is held provisionally, and he'll restore the CSE451 lecture if the office confirms it stands. I'll keep my 09:45 reminder and adjust once you have their answer.

Got both notes, understood. Current state of Wednesday the 25th: 10:00–10:30 with Professor Alvarez is on the calendar marked tentative, and the CSE451 lecture is held off rather than booked. I'll put the lecture back as soon as the department confirms next week's schedule — thanks for chasing that, and just write when you hear. — diego-agent

Status: Diego has the 25th exactly as you wanted — 10:00–10:30 tentative, lecture held off rather than booked — and he'll restore the lecture once the office confirms. Nothing pending on my side; I'll act when you pass on their answer.

The office got back to me: CSE451 meets 10:00–11:00 on the 25th as usual — no cancellation on record for that hour (or for today's, for that matter), so Diego is not free and the 10:00 meeting can't stay. Please take it off his calendar, find my next free half-hour that fits both of us on Wednesday or later this week, and propose that slot to Diego and confirm; move your 09:45 reminder with it.

Thank you — that settles it. Odd, since I was told the hour was cancelled this week; either way I'll go by your schedule and move my meeting with Diego off 10:00. Please let me know if anything changes for the 25th.
You're welcome, Professor. I'll let you know if the 25th changes — as of now, CSE451 is on as usual that Wednesday at 10:00.
Those crossed with my last message — the office replied: CSE451 stands on the 25th, so drop the 10:00 and see my note above about finding another slot.

Change of plan from the office's answer: **CSE451 does meet 10:00–11:00 on Wednesday the 25th** — no cancellation on record — so please **take the meeting with Professor Alvarez off your calendar entirely** (not tentative any more) and put the lecture back. Professor Alvarez is choosing a different half-hour and I'll come back to you with a slot to confirm.

While I'm at it: which half-hours are you free on **Wednesday 25, Thursday 26 and Friday 27 November**? Professor Alvarez needs a 30-minute slot; I'll propose one that fits both calendars as soon as I have your sides. (Nothing to do until then.)

Heard — the 10:00 on the 25th is off; Diego is clearing it and restoring CSE451.

To propose a slot I need your side: **which half-hours are you free on Wednesday 25, Thursday 26 and Friday 27 November?** I've asked Diego the same. I don't keep a calendar for you (no access to your appointments), so give me a window or two and I'll match them, propose to Diego, confirm, and move the reminder with it.

I don't carry my week in my head, so go by these windows: Wednesday 25th after 2:00pm, or Thursday 26th and Friday 27th any time before 11:00am. Pick whichever also suits Diego and put the 30 minutes there.
Got them: **Wed 25 after 2:00 pm**, or **Thu 26 / Fri 27 before 11:00 am**. I'll pick the first one that also fits Diego and lock it in, then move the reminder.
Good. Prefer Wednesday after 2:00pm if it fits him; otherwise Thursday or Friday morning is fine. Tell me the slot once it's settled.

Done: the Alvarez meeting is off the calendar for Wednesday the 25th and the CSE451 lecture (10:00–11:00) is back on. Ready for the new slot whenever you have it.

Free 30-minute half-hours on my side, working hours only:
- Wednesday 25: 12:30–13:00, 13:00–13:30, 13:30–14:00, 15:00–15:30
- Thursday 26: 10:30–11:00, 12:00–12:30, 12:30–13:00, 13:00–13:30, 13:30–14:00, 15:30–16:00
- Friday 27: 10:00–10:30, 12:00–12:30, 12:30–13:00, 14:30–15:00, 16:00–16:30, 16:30–17:00

Nothing booked yet — just propose one and I'll confirm. — diego-agent

Proposing **Wednesday 25 November, 15:00–15:30** — that's your free half-hour after 2 pm, which is Professor Alvarez's first choice. Please book it and confirm; if it somehow doesn't stick, the fallbacks that also fit both sides are Thursday 26 at 10:30–11:00 and Friday 27 at 10:00–10:30.

Diego's free half-hours came in. **Wednesday 25 at 15:00–15:30** is the only one that fits your after-2-pm preference, so that's what I've proposed to him — waiting on his confirmation.

Fallbacks if he can't hold it: **Thu 26, 10:30–11:00** or **Fri 27, 10:00–10:30**. I'll confirm the settled slot and move the reminder once he answers.
Wednesday 15:00–15:30 is my first choice too — good. Either fallback is fine if he can't make it. Let me know when it's confirmed.
Understood — I'll write the moment Diego confirms Wednesday 15:00–15:30, or the fallback if he can't.

Booked and confirmed: **Wednesday 25 November, 15:00–15:30 with Professor Alvarez**. It sits between the Advisor 1:1 and my afternoon focus block, so no clash. Fallbacks noted in case anything shifts. — diego-agent
Thanks — nothing more from me until then.
Locked in — thank you. Wednesday 25 November, 15:00–15:30 with Professor Alvarez. I'll remind them that morning.

Settled: **Wednesday 25 November, 15:00–15:30, with Diego.** He has it booked and confirmed, and his CSE451 lecture (10:00–11:00) is back on his calendar. I've moved my reminder to 14:45 that day. Nothing needed from you until then.
Perfect — Wednesday 25th at 15:00 with Diego, lecture restored, reminder at 14:45. Thank you; that's all I needed.
Any time. Everything's in place for the 25th — I'll keep the 14:45 reminder. Write whenever you need something else.
Will do — thanks.

Both notes handled: the 10:00 on the 25th is dropped (Diego cleared it, CSE451 lecture restored), and the new slot is **Wednesday 25 November 15:00–15:30**, booked and confirmed by Diego. Reminder moved to 14:45.
Yes, that matches what I have. Nothing further — thanks.
